messages:
maria: quick q about the embeddings endpoint — want to lock down a few contract details before we add more e2e tests. Specifically: char encoding (non-utf8 bytes?), empty strings/nulls, whether truncation is by characters or tokens, and per-request batch limits. also saw a PR that touched normalization — did we change that behavior?

aj: re: encoding, our clients usually send UTF-8. if someone sends arbitrary bytes what happens? db/ingest might generate weird stuff.

embed-bot: heads-up: recent deploy (canary) rolled embedding model update to redwood-embed-large-v1. No contract changes intended. Docs: https://redwood.example/docs/embeddings#input-contract

aj: thanks — will avoid pushing weird bytes in tests for now.

simon: digging in — short answers first, then examples.

1) input types: endpoint accepts either a single string or a JSON array of strings. we canonicalize by wrapping a lone string into a 1-element list. we do NOT accept raw binary blobs. clients should UTF-8 encode text; if you send invalid utf-8 the request will be rejected with 400 ("invalid encoding").

2) empty vs null: empty string ("") => returns a valid vector (model embedding for empty text). we intentionally return a deterministic vector (not all-zeros) for empty string to avoid ambiguity in similarity pipelines. null (JSON null) or missing elements => 400 with message "null input not allowed; use empty string to represent blank content".

3) truncation: token-based using the model tokenizer. we truncate at token boundary, not at character boundary, to preserve tokenization semantics. per-input max tokens = 8192 for redwood-embed-large-v1; if input exceeds that we truncate the tail. we include a response header X-Embed-Truncated: true when any input was truncated.

4) batch limits: max 512 items per request AND total-token budget per request = 200000 tokens. the server enforces both. if either limit is exceeded you get 413 with details. recommend clients chunk by number of items and by token count; we provide a lightweight client helper for chunking in the SDK.

5) output shape and ordering: response returns "data": [ {"embedding": [...], "index": i } ] in the same order as the canonicalized inputs. index mirrors the input index so you can reorder or correlate results easily. embedding dimension for redwood-embed-large-v1 = 1536. every item is a list of floats.

6) normalization/backwards compatibility: default behavior remains the same as prior release: embeddings are L2-normalized before return. we intentionally did NOT change default normalization in the canary. there will be an opt-in query param `?raw=true` coming in the next minor which returns pre-normalized vectors (useful for some approximate indexes). we'll announce as a minor semver bump and call that out in changelog.

examples:
```bash
# single string (server wraps to list)
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{ "input": "hello world", "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1" }

# batch
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "input": ["a","b","c"], "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1" }
```

error examples:
- sending binary or invalid UTF-8 => 400 invalid encoding
- sending JSON null in array => 400 null input not allowed
- >512 items => 413 too many items (see limits)
- >200k total tokens => 413 token budget exceeded

natalie: small question — you said empty string returns deterministic vector, could that break semantics where ppl expect zeros? our similarity code currently treats "" as special-case and maps to zeros.

simon: good catch. we intentionally removed the zeros behavior in v2 because it made few downstream operations ambiguous (empty docs clustered with unrelated docs). for migration: we'll add a compatibility flag `empty_is_zero=true` for 2 releases. default remains deterministic non-zero vector. we'll add a guide to the migration doc.

maria: perfect — i'll add tests for: invalid utf8 -> 400, null in array -> 400, >512 items -> 413, per-item token truncation header, and embedding dim == 1536. i'll also update our ingest pipeline to force utf-8 and to avoid converting empty -> null.

aj: i'll add SDK chunking helper to wrap by tokens+count. ping me for review.

simon: thanks all. i'll open a short RFC/PR to document X-Embed-Truncated header and the empty_is_zero compatibility flag. linking to draft: https://redwood.example/rfcs/embeddings-truncation-2026

maria: awesome, thanks. :thumbsup:

embed-bot: deploy scheduled for next stable (no breaking changes).

maria: closing loop — will post test PR once done.

(reacts: :eyes: on simon's RFC)
